Diego —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our leadership signed off in principle on moving a portion of our traffic to Redwood Dedicated for production. Before procurement can finish we need a short mutual action plan and an agreed stress-validation window that proves performance under our P95/P99 targets and peak concurrency.

Quick facts from our side:
- Baseline traffic: 250 qps average (2k tokens req avg)
- Peak bursts observed: 1.1k qps sustained ~2–3 min, spike-testing up to ~1.8k qps for <30s
- Target p95 latency <= 120 ms, p99 <= 280 ms (inference-only)
- Current hosted spend per token: cite in procurement request

Immediate asks:
1) Can you put together a short MAP with milestones and acceptance gates?
2) Proposed stress-test protocol and test dataset (we can share an anonymized corpus)
3) A recommended GPU reservation window (days/hours) for a staging stress run + production canary

I'll loop in PlatformOps (platform@asteriahealth.com) once we have dates. Procurement wants the MAP attached to the PO.

-Sarah

Appreciate the clear notes. Attached is a first pass MAP (MAP-Asteria-Health-v3.pdf) and our redwood-stress-protocol-v2.md. High-level proposal:

- Sizing assumption (initial): 8x A100 equivalent GPUs (mixed split: 6 inference, 2 warm/encoder preproc) based on your baseline + 2x headroom for bursts.
- Staging stress window (recommended): 2026-08-28 09:00 PT → 2026-08-29 18:00 PT (two half-day stress windows to sweep concurrency & batch tuning)
- Canary: 2026-08-30 10:00 PT (2-hour canary ramp to 30% traffic, monitor p95/p99 and error rate)
- Acceptance gates: p95 <= 120ms AND p99 <= 300ms AND <0.3% 5xx errors during canary
- Rollback: automatic traffic cut to hosted with warm KV cache fallback if errors exceed threshold; procurement hold-out clause for billing adjustments if baseline costs deviate by >15%

Deliverables we will provide: MAP PDF, stress protocol, runbook for cutover and rollback, and a quick trace dashboard link for the canary. We recommend the stress run use your anonymized dataset; please upload to the shared drive link in this thread.

Ask for PlatformOps and procurement: confirm the PO cadence and whether you need Redwood to push a contract amendment before the stress window.

I'll also route this to SEs to validate the 8 GPU baseline and run a pre-flight staging stress this week.

Diego —

Quick update from staging stress sweep (see attachment stress-results-20260824.csv). Run notes:
- Test points run: 250 qps, 500 qps, 1k qps, 1.5k qps (10m sustained each), brief spike to 1.8k for 30s.
- p95 observations: 250 qps = 88ms, 500 qps = 110ms, 1k qps = 155ms, 1.5k qps = 260ms
- p99 observations: 250 qps = 160ms, 500 qps = 220ms, 1k qps = 360ms, 1.5k qps = 710ms (sustained queueing noted)
- Bottleneck: preprocessing workers (tokenization & input mapping) saturated earlier than GPU. CPU-bound latency under burst; GPU memory headroom looked ok.

Recommendations:
1) Increase recommended baseline to 10x A100-eq (or split: 8 inference + 2 dedicated preproc nodes with 64GB CPUs) to meet p99 under 1.5k sustained.
2) Add a short warmup period (60s) before canary ramp to prime KV cache; reduces p99 by ~12% in repeated runs.
3) For cost control, we can offer a quantized variant usable during off-peak with expected ~3% quality delta on the validation set; attach quantization notes in the stress CSV comments.

Proposed canary schedule (finalized): 2026-08-30 10:00–12:00 PT (ramp to 30% traffic over 20 minutes, hold for 90 minutes). If canary passes gates, plan production cutover 2026-09-02 01:00 PT (low-traffic window).

I'll open a staging reservation ticket with infra. Priyom — can you confirm SOC2 audit artifact packaging & that the dedicated environment will have audit logging turned on (we should include a short note for procurement)?

-Marissa
